# The Shadow the Earth Casts

## Scripture
*"You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden."* — Matthew 5:14 (ESV)

## Reflection
On a clear November night, if the Moon passes through Earth's shadow, we witness a lunar eclipse. The Moon doesn't vanish—it glows a deep copper-red, lit by sunlight bending through our atmosphere. Even in shadow, light finds a way.

Here's what strikes me: that reddish glow comes from every sunrise and sunset on Earth happening at once, refracted onto the Moon's face. The Moon shines not with its own light but with borrowed light—and even our planet's shadow can't fully extinguish it.

Jesus told His followers they were the light of the world. Not the sun—that's His role. More like the Moon: reflective, dependent, shining with light that isn't our own. And sometimes we pass through seasons of shadow—weariness, doubt, hiddenness. We feel eclipsed.

But notice: an eclipsed Moon is still fully present. Still held in orbit. Still reflecting, however dimly. God doesn't abandon us in the shadow; He redeems it, bending even our darkest seasons into something that glows with unexpected warmth.

This fall, when the nights stretch long, remember: you were never meant to generate your own light. You were meant to reflect His. And no shadow—not even Earth's own—can separate you from the One who holds you in orbit.

## Prayer
Lord, when I pass through seasons of shadow, remind me that I am still held, still seen, still Yours. Let Your light bend through my circumstances and shine—even faintly—so others might glimpse Your glory. Amen.
